The middling … the sublime … that which is dominated by desire … [and so forth] … 1086. The mind becomes concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability; and he applies and directs it to the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions. This too is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, and it is higher and more sublime than the former one. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, and it is higher and more sublime than the former one. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, and it is higher and more sublime than the former one. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, and it is higher and more sublime than the former one. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, by completely transcending the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling. And this—by realising for oneself with direct knowledge—comes to be where these meritorious things come to fulfilment by development. 1087. “There are, bhikkhus, other noble abidings here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which are higher and more sublime than this. And what are they? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings as feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind as mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells detached from sense-desires, detached from unwholesome states, and so on, he enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of detachment. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, enters upon and abides in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, with the fading away as well of rapture, dwells equanimous and, mindful and clearly comprehending, he experiences pleasure with the body; he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna, on account of which the Noble Ones announce: ‘He dwells pleasantly, mindful, and equanimous. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. And what is that? Here, bhikkhus, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness. This is a noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture. But this noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, is surpassed by another noble abiding here and now, pleasant, and not devoid of rapture, which is higher and more sublime than it. ...the middling ... the sublime ... that which is dominated by investigation ... the inferior ... [and so forth] ... 1084. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal form, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external form, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1085. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1086. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal earth element, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external earth element, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1087. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal water element, fire element, air element, space element, or consciousness element, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external water element, fire element, air element, space element, or consciousness element, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1088. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1089. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external visible forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1090. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, or mind-consciousness, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object? It is whatever external eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the external object. 1091. Therein, what is the internal object? It is whatever internal feeling born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact, whether past, future, or present, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, that is the basis for the arising of lust or for the arising of unwholesome states. This is called the internal object. What is the external object?
